phases.name: Define the puzzle
phases.asks: Ask a consequential question with little, conflicting, or incomplete theory/evidence; do not pre-specify the relationships to be discovered.
phases.output: Research question, initial construct sensitizers, contribution target, prior-theory proximity.
phases.failure: Declaring a generic “gap” while implicitly fixing the answer in advance.

phases.name: Design theoretical variation
phases.asks: Choose cases because the phenomenon is present and because similarities/differences can reveal or challenge theoretical patterns. Designs can include matched pairs, polar types, racing cases, and embedded replications.
phases.output: Case-selection matrix, inclusion logic, expected replication/contrast, alternative-explanation controls.
phases.failure: Convenience sampling relabeled as theoretical sampling.

phases.name: Build case evidence
phases.asks: Combine sources appropriate to the question; qualitative, quantitative, archival, observational, or mixed evidence are all permitted. Preserve chronology and provenance.
phases.output: Case database, source/provenance map, event chronology, construct-evidence table.
phases.failure: Treating interview quotations as the only legitimate data, or losing source-level traceability.

phases.name: Analyze each case as a case
phases.asks: Establish the internal story, event sequence, constructs, and candidate relationships before pooling attention across cases.
phases.output: Within-case narrative/chronology, provisional constructs, disconfirming evidence, confidence notes.
phases.failure: Jumping directly to themes across interviews and erasing case context.

phases.name: Compare across cases
phases.asks: Use multiple lenses and deliberate pairings; examine replication, contradiction, presence/absence, sequence, equifinality, and qualitative differences.
phases.output: Cross-case matrix, replication/contradiction ledger, revised construct definitions.
phases.failure: Counting surface similarities without asking why patterns occur.

phases.name: Build mechanisms and theory
phases.asks: Link constructs through explicit theoretical arguments, test rival explanations, and state boundary conditions.
phases.output: Parsimonious model, propositions where useful, mechanism ledger, rival-explanation table, boundary conditions.
phases.failure: Presenting a category taxonomy or data display as if it were explanatory theory.

phases.name: Iterate with data and literature
phases.asks: Revisit cases and relevant literatures to sharpen constructs, reveal novelty, improve internal validity, and locate contribution; theory elaboration/abduction is allowed.
phases.output: Theory–evidence revisions, literature contrast table, negative-case responses.
phases.failure: Claiming a literal blank slate or adding citations only after analysis as decoration.

phases.name: Stop and communicate
phases.asks: Stop when additional evidence no longer materially improves the theoretical account, while also acknowledging pragmatic limits; justify case count rather than invoke a magic number.
phases.output: Saturation/stopping memo, residual uncertainty, testable implications, transparent methods narrative.
phases.failure: Treating “4–10 cases” or “about eight” as a rule.

core: Theory building is the organizing aim; constructs alone are insufficient without relationships and why-mechanisms.
Cases are theoretical replications and analytic units, not observations pooled under statistical sampling logic.
Careful case selection creates theoretically useful similarity and difference and helps address alternative explanations.
Constant comparison, within-case analysis, cross-case analysis, literature iteration, boundary conditions, and theoretical arguments work as one system.
The desired theory balances parsimony, empirical accuracy, logical coherence, testability, and relevance beyond the immediate setting.
folklore: A fixed count of cases. Four to ten is a historically common range, not a rule.
Interviews or qualitative data only. Archival, quantitative, observational, ethnographic, and mixed evidence may be appropriate.
Variance theory rather than process theory.
A rigid positivist philosophy or a fully detached researcher.
A standardized visual data structure analogous to the Gioia display.

demarcation.target: Explanatory theory: constructs, relationships, mechanisms, and boundaries across cases
demarcation.warrant: Theoretical sampling plus within/cross-case constant comparison and replication logic

demarcation.target: Informant-grounded concepts and a transparent progression from first-order terms to second-order themes and a grounded model
demarcation.warrant: Informant-centric coding, data structure, and traceable movement from participant terms to researcher concepts
demarcation.relation: Shares induction and iteration, but foregrounds informant meaning and coding architecture; it should not be treated as the same workflow.

demarcation.target: Case-study design, evidence convergence, and analytic replication for explanatory or deductive as well as exploratory studies
demarcation.warrant: Case protocol, multiple sources, replication logic, chain of evidence
demarcation.relation: Supplies much of the case and replication logic that Eisenhardt integrates into inductive theory building.

demarcation.target: Theory generated through theoretical sampling, constant comparison, and saturation
demarcation.warrant: Iterative category/theory development grounded in data
demarcation.relation: Supplies core inductive logic; Eisenhardt adds a particularly explicit multi-case comparison and theoretical-argument architecture.

demarcation.target: Explanations of how phenomena unfold over time using multiple process-theorizing strategies
demarcation.warrant: Temporal patterning, sequencing, narrative/visual/bracketing and related strategies
demarcation.relation: Complementary rather than categorically opposed; Eisenhardt 2021 explicitly embraces time and process possibilities.

demarcationNote: Combining techniques is defensible only when the research question, assumptions, unit of analysis, and output logic remain coherent. A paper that cites all approaches but merely borrows their visible reporting devices has not established method fit.
missing: within-case event chronologies and evidence provenance
cross-case replication, contradiction, and negative-case tests
